chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who performs ziyarah (visitation) and sleeps before Mina, he said: 'When he has passed the pass of the Madinin, there is no harm in him sleeping.'

key_terms.عَقَبَةَ الْمَدِينِيِّينَ: The pass of the Madinin, a specific geographical landmark in the Hajj route
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend days of Hajj

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible for a pilgrim to sleep before reaching Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of resting during the Hajj journey, specifically after passing the 'Aqabah of the Madinin, a key landmark on the route to Mina. It reflects the practical flexibility (rukhsah) granted to pilgrims to manage fatigue without compromising the ritual integrity of their visit to the Kaaba. The ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease in worship, ensuring that physical needs do not become an undue burden during the sacred rites.
